title: The MCU-MECOM Axis Orchestrates Glioblastoma Progression by Remodeling Mitochondrial Dynamics and Quality Control via MAMs.
authors: Li, Xiaodong; Wang, Yaoliang; Wu, Feifei; Huang, Xin; Ni, Ziwei; Xu, Guangzhen; Wang, Weizhong; Tie, Jingjing; Huang, Yunqiang; Sun, Yuze; Wang, Zhenhua; Li, Shujiao; Zheng, Qianwen; Liu, Yuxuan; Wu, Yousheng; Gong, Chengrong; Guo, Qingdong; Yang, Yanling; Wang, Yayun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胶质母细胞瘤中MCU-MECOM轴通过线粒体相关膜重塑代谢，虽含转录因子MECOM和深度学习工具MAMs-Net，但核心是线粒体钙代谢与肿瘤机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits metabolic plasticity, relying on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to support migration and therapy resistance. Although mitochondrial calcium overload typically induces apoptosis, GBM cells maintain viability under high calcium conditions. The structural and metabolic coupling mechanisms underlying this adaptation remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs) regulatory axis driven by a positive feedback loop between the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and the transcription factor MECOM. Using multi-omics profiling, time-resolved functional assays, and mitochondrial transfer experiments, we show that MCU-mediated calcium influx expands MAMs without triggering cell death. This influx initiates adaptive mitochondrial cristae remodeling via the Mic10/Mic60 complex and activates selective mitophagy. Pharmacological blockade and autophagy-rescue experiments (using si-ATG5 and chloroquine) indicate that this mitophagy-dependent quality control promotes tumor migration and buffers reactive oxygen species (ROS) to sustain OXPHOS capacity. Targeting the MCU-MECOM axis induces metabolic suppression and reduces glioma cell viability. To translate these findings into a diagnostic application, we developed MAMs-Net, a deep-learning framework for the automated quantification of MAMs ultrastructure from transmission electron microscope (TEM) images. In an independent external validation cohort, MAMs-Net achieved an AUC of 0.95 for glioma pathological stratification. This study characterizes an MCU-MECOM structural-metabolic circuit that supports GBM survival under calcium overload, identifying a potential therapeutic target and providing a pathophysiologically interpretable, AI-driven tool for glioma evaluation.
abstract_zh: 胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）表现出代谢可塑性，依赖线粒体氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）来支持迁移和治疗抵抗。尽管线粒体钙超载通常诱导细胞凋亡，但GBM细胞在高钙条件下仍能维持活力。这种适应背后的结构和代谢偶联机制尚未完全阐明。在此，我们鉴定了一个由线粒体钙单向转运体（MCU）与转录因子MECOM之间的正反馈环路驱动的线粒体相关膜（MAMs）调控轴。利用多组学分析、时间分辨功能实验和线粒体转移实验，我们证明MCU介导的钙内流扩展了MAMs而不触发细胞死亡。该内流通过Mic10/Mic60复合物启动适应性线粒体嵴重塑，并激活选择性线粒体自噬。药理学阻断和自噬拯救实验（使用si-ATG5和氯喹）表明，这种依赖线粒体自噬的质量控制促进肿瘤迁移，并缓冲活性氧（ROS）以维持OXPHOS能力。靶向MCU-MECOM轴可诱导代谢抑制并降低胶质瘤细胞活力。为将这些发现转化为诊断应用，我们开发了MAMs-Net，一种用于从透射电子显微镜（TEM）图像自动量化MAMs超微结构的深度学习框架。在独立外部验证队列中，MAMs-Net在胶质瘤病理分层中达到了0.95的AUC。本研究表征了一个支持GBM在钙超载下存活的MCU-MECOM结构-代谢回路，确定了潜在的治疗靶点，并提供了具有病理生理学可解释性的AI驱动工具用于胶质瘤评估。
